evaluation_schema_recovery.initial_failure: V63 centered ensemble schema was absent from the evaluator CENTERED_SCHEMAS set, causing an attempted read of legacy high-pass attributes before any metric was written
evaluation_schema_recovery.fix: register the V63 ensemble as the same DC-centered full-band residual family as V50 and V52

scientific_conclusion: The V63 conditional moment objective is causal and substantially better than V50 and V52: all three frozen extreme diagnostics improve against both references in every development domain, while the rolled-parameter control is much worse.

The repair is nevertheless not development sufficient. SIMBA passes Q3, Q4, and every field check, but TNG100 fails the maximum-excess part of Q3 and one 0-1 Mpc/h two-point comparison; Swift narrowly exceeds the q99.999 and mean-moment limits and also fails the maximum-excess part of Q3.
Every high-k power and residual-RMS check passes. The remaining failure is not the prior small-filament smoothing problem and is not a quadrature, DC, inverse-CDF, or provenance failure.

The train gate calibrates quadrature expectations, whereas the development gate measures fields produced by a finite frozen empirical-rank transport. The next justified question is whether this sampler-to-objective mismatch is measurable and gradient-bearing on train-only data before authorizing another fit.
